title: SLO-first accelerator matching with per-tenant budget slices and spot/on-demand arbitration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a routing policy that prioritizes tenant SLOs (p95 latency, availability) while honoring per-tenant budget slices. The controller should choose region and accelerator class (A100, H100, L4, or CPU) and decide spot vs on-demand for each request class. Goal: minimize cost without violating latency/availability SLOs and provide configurable soft/hard spend caps per tenant. The policy must expose controls in Console, emit clear telemetry for cost vs quality trade-offs, and provide safe fallback model variant selection when preemption or capacity failures occur.
background: Customers run a mixture of latency-sensitive and throughput-oriented workloads. We currently route largely by static priority and SKU affinity, which leads to either excessive spend (over-provision to meet SLOs) or SLO violations when spot eviction rates spike. Previous tickets explored budgeted routing and graceful degradation, but lacked a single SLO-first arbitration layer that ties per-request runtime constraints to accelerator suitability and live spot risk signals.
design_decisions: 1) SLO-first scoring: compute a per-request score combining remaining latency headroom, model short-name compatibility, and kernel fit score for candidate accelerator classes. 2) Budget slices: each tenant exposes a monthly budget slice and a realtime soft/spend burn rate. Soft cap allows opportunistic spot use until a projected overrun threshold; hard cap triggers strict on-demand-only routing or throttling. 3) Spot arbitration: use an eviction-risk signal from infra + cloud spot market estimator to compute a spot-risk multiplier. For high spot-risk or tight latency headroom, prefer on-demand SKUs. 4) Accelerator matching: prefer lower-cost SKUs only when kernel suitability score passes threshold; otherwise route to higher class to meet p95. 5) Fallback variants: when primary model on target SKU cannot meet SLO or is preempted, automatically route to certified quantized or distilled variant with a configured degradation budget. 6) Burst credits: support short-term burst allowance (credits) which can be consumed to temporarily exceed soft cap with higher cost to preserve SLO-critical traffic.
tradeoffs: - Strict enforcement of hard caps can cause availability regressions for critical tenants. We mitigate this with prioritized critical buckets and emergency contact hooks. - Aggressive use of spot reduces cost but increases tail latency variance; requires improved telemetry and fallback coverage. - Kernel suitability scoring increases scheduling complexity and slightly increases route decision latency; we will cache scores and precompute model->accelerator matrices offline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end routing path selects accelerator and pricing class (spot/on-demand) for 95% of requests within 10ms decision latency under peak load. 2) P95 latency for SLO-tagged queries does not regress >5% compared to baseline when burst credits not used. 3) Cost delta: tenant spend decreases by >=10% for medium-to-high spot-eligible workloads in internal canary. 4) Console exposes tenant soft/hard caps and historical projection chart. 5) Automated fallback selects compatible model variant in <200ms on preemption events.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: scoring engine + offline model->accelerator matrix (2 weeks). Phase 2: budget-slice service and console knobs (2 weeks). Phase 3: spot-risk adapter and decision point integration into request router (3 weeks). Phase 4: fallback variant registry and graceful switch logic + integration tests (2 weeks). Phase 5: canary roll, metrics validation, and iterative tuning (2 weeks). Total estimated sprint count: 3 sprints.
tests: - Unit tests for scoring math and budget projection simulation. - Load test: 50k RPS synthetic mix with varying eviction traces to validate decision latency and p95. - Fault injection: force spot eviction and region outage to validate fallback model variant selection and route replanning. - Cost simulation: run month-long synthetic workload to verify spend projection and soft/hard cap behavior. - Integration test with Console UI toggles and RBAC to ensure visibility and safety.
telemetry_metrics: List of primary metrics to emit: 'routing.decision_latency_ms', 'routing.selected_accelerator', 'routing.pricing_class', 'tenant.spend_projection_pct', 'tenant.spend_status' (OK|SOFT_EXCEEDED|HARD_BLOCKED), 'fallback.activation.count', 'spot_eviction_rate', 'p95_latency.slo_tagged'. Alerts: tenant.spend_status HARD_BLOCKED, fallback.rate > 0.5% for >10m, p95_latency increase >10% vs baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha with engineering tenants only behind feature flag. 2) Small customer canary (3 customers) with manual monitoring. 3) Gradual ramp with automated rollback if alerts fire. 4) Default policy: disabled for all tenants until 2-week canary green and PM signoff. 5) Post-rollout: enable soft-caps by default but keep hard-caps opt-in.
risks: - Incorrect kernel suitability scoring could route compute-heavy models to insufficient hardware, causing errors. Mitigation: conservative thresholds + quick metrics lookback to revert. - Billing disputes when soft cap bursts happen: require explicit Console consent and billing note on invoices. - Complexity in scheduler could add median decision latency; mitigate by caching and using batched scoring.
open_questions: 1) Do we expose automatic conversion of tenant budgets to burst credits or require manual purchase? 2) What granularity for spend slices (monthly vs weekly vs daily) is most valuable to customers? 3) Should hard cap trigger throttling or fallback-only behavior for critical customers? Invite PM decision. 4) How aggressive should the spot-risk multiplier be in early canary?
notes_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting; alignment with Runtime team on kernel scoring format. 2026-02-23: Prototype of model->accelerator matrix completed by infra-research; early scoring shows H100 benefits for long-context models but L4 cost wins for small chat models. 2026-03-01: PM request to surface cost-projection chart in Console before canary. 2026-03-06: Design feedback from Design: prefer 'soft cap' wording 'buffer allowance' in UI copy. 2026-03-10: Infra team validated spot eviction estimator; integration tests scheduled for 2026-03-18.
implementation_notes: - Scoring will be implemented as an independent service 'route-evaluator' with gRPC interface. - Use Redis TTL cache for recent model->accelerator scores. - Add protobufs for pricing_class and accelerator enum to runtime contract. - Ensure canary flag toggles both routing logic and Console controls.
final_notes: This ticket centralizes existing cost-aware heuristics into an SLO-first arbitration layer with explicit budget semantics. The feature will enable teams to get lower unit costs while keeping tight latency targets and providing transparent controls for tenants.
